predictions.source_summary: URI and image_id come from authenticated API delete requests after authorization checks. URI from image['location'], image_id from request path parameter.
predictions.sink_summary: Creates files in CONF.scrubber_datadir with image_id as filename, containing URI and deletion timestamp. Uses os.chmod(0600) and os.utime to set permissions and access times.
predictions.guard_summary: API-level: _enforce('delete_image') authorization, protected image check. Function-level: duplicate file check raises exception.Duplicate. File permissions set to 0600 (owner read/write only).
predictions.risk_pattern: Scheduled deletion creates files with predictable names (image_id) in configurable directory. Potential race condition between existence check and file creation. File permissions may be insufficient if directory permissions allow access.
predictions.context_summary: Function implements delayed deletion by writing deletion queue files. Called from authenticated API endpoints after authorization checks. Creates files with image_id as filename containing URI and scheduled deletion time.
unresolved_facts: Whether scrubber_datadir directory permissions are properly secured
Whether image_id values are predictable or can be manipulated
Whether race condition between existence check and file creation is exploitable
Whether v2 API bug using 'id' instead of 'image_id' affects functionality

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
top_sast_rules.description: Extracting files from a potentially malicious tarball using `shutil.unpack_archive()` without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can cause files outside the destination directory to be overwritten. More precisely, if the tarball comes from a user controlled location either a remote one or cli argument.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement path validation using canonical paths. Reject paths containing '../' or similar traversal sequences.

top_sast_rules.description: Legacy access-control category for failures in permissions, privileges, or authorization enforcement.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-264 permissions privileges access-control authorization acl role privilege owner permission enforcement
top_sast_rules.remediation: Enforce trusted authorization, role, ownership, and permission checks.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
top_sast_rules.description: File access follows a symlink, hardlink, or shortcut to an unintended resource.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-59 symlink hardlink link-following symbolic-link file-link archive-extraction path-resolution file-overwrite race filesystem
top_sast_rules.remediation: Reject unsafe links and verify resolved file targets before access.

top_sast_rules.description: An access-control policy is missing or incorrectly enforced for a protected resource.

top_sast_rules.description: When checking a Hash over a message, a constant-time algorithm should be used. Otherwise, an attacker may be able to forge a valid Hash for an arbitrary message by running a timing attack if they can send to the validation procedure. A successful attack can result in authentication bypass.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Use constant-time algorithms for sensitive comparisons. Implement timing attack mitigations for authentication and cryptographic operations.
